instruction: CORRECTNESS R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020Q (conflict-gate suppression-path corpus + Python waiver-awareness, closes TF-006) at branch feature/wp-scp-022-020q-conflict-gate-suppression-corpus, HEAD commit 05cab6d. Verify CORRECTNESS exhaustively. The slice translates policies/scp_common.rego suppression helpers to Python and adds 5 new fixtures exercising both engines. Specifically: (1) Read policies/scp_common.rego AND tests/conflict_gate/test_conflict_gate.py at HEAD. Verify the Python translations match the Rego semantics 1:1, predicate by predicate: (a) _parse_dateish_ns vs scp_dateish_ns (lines 94-104) — both regexes (YYYY-MM-DD anchored; RFC3339 with explicit timezone); both treat YYYY-MM-DD as midnight UTC; both reject anything else. Verify the Python YYYY-MM-DD path constructs datetime in UTC; the RFC3339 path normalises 'Z' → '+00:00' (Python <3.11 limitation; safe on 3.11+ too); both return integer ns or None. (b) _scp_waiver_expired vs scp_waiver_expired (lines 54-72) — fail-closed on missing/empty/unparseable expires_at; expired when expiry_ns <= now_ns. Verify the three Rego clauses are all covered. (c) _scp_active_waiver_for vs scp_active_waiver_for (lines 44-49) — iterates waivers; matches rule_id only (no finding_id matching per scp_common.rego comment lines 36-43); returns True iff any matching, non-expired entry. Verify the Python iteration semantics match Rego's `some w in scp_waivers` quantifier. (d) _scp_rule_config_disabled vs scp_rule_config_disabled (lines 77-81) — checks rule_config.rules[rule_id].disable == True; False on any missing key (mirrors `default scp_rule_config_disabled := false`). Verify Python returns False on type mismatch at every level. (2) _load_sibling_waivers / _load_sibling_rule_config — verify they handle (a) missing file → []/{}; (b) malformed JSON/YAML → []/{}; (c) wrong root type → []/{}; (d) yaml.safe_load is used (NOT yaml.load — RCE risk). (3) _build_opa_data_arg — verify (a) returns None when no siblings exist (callers skip --data); (b) tempfile is created in a stable location with a stable prefix; (c) tempfile carries `{"waivers": [...], "rule_config": {...}}` matching the namespaces scp_common.rego reads; (d) tempfile is unlinked on exception during write. (4) _run_opa changes — verify (a) command construction is correct: --data <rule>.rego --data scp_common.rego --data <tempfile-if-any> --input <fixture> 'data.main.deny'; (b) tempfile cleanup is in finally block (cleans up even if subprocess raises); (c) existing fixtures (allow/deny without siblings) still produce the same opa command (no --data tempfile flag); (d) the tempfile path is passed correctly to OPA's --data flag (basename matters for the data tree namespace — verify '_scp_test_data_' prefix doesn't collide with anything in scp_common.rego's expected paths). (5) _suppression_active — verify it loads waivers + rule_config from scenario_dir and returns True iff either suppression applies. Now is computed via datetime.now(tz=utc).timestamp() * 1e9 — integer truncation matches scp_now_ns granularity. (6) Per-evaluator changes — verify _evaluate_scp_r_001_python, _evaluate_scp_r_002_python, _evaluate_scp_r_004_python all check _suppression_active BEFORE evaluating findings, return {"findings": []} on suppression. SCP-R-003 unchanged (no Python equivalent). (7) New fixture: SCP-R-001/waiver-suppressed — input.yml has unapproved mode; waivers.json has active SCP-R-001 waiver with far-future expires_at; expected-verdict.json says allow. Verify the waiver shape matches the rest of the corpus (W-CG-FIXTURE prefix; @jrnb2024 approved_by; reason carries a URL per SCP-R-004 v1.1.0). (8) New fixture: SCP-R-001/waiver-expired — input.yml unapproved mode; waivers.json with expires_at in 2024 (past); expected-verdict.json says **deny**. Verify both engines apply fail-closed. (9) New fixture: SCP-R-001/rule-config-disabled — input.yml unapproved mode; .scp/rule-config.yaml with rules.SCP-R-001.disable: true; expected-verdict.json says allow. Verify the YAML is valid and matches the schemas/rule-config.schema.json shape. (10) New fixture: SCP-R-002/waiver-suppressed — input.json has malformed waiver entry (missing reason); waivers.json has meta-waiver targeting SCP-R-002 with URL-bearing reason; expected-verdict.json says allow. (11) New fixture: SCP-R-004/waiver-suppressed — input.json has waiver missing URL in reason; waivers.json has meta-waiver targeting SCP-R-004 with URL-bearing reason; expected-verdict.json says allow. (12) Verify all 11 fixtures (6 existing + 5 new) actually pass via the conflict-gate test driver. The pre-commit smoke test confirmed 11/11 pass — verify the test logic that produces this is correct (no false-pass paths). (13) .gitignore changes — verify the negation rule actually works (`!tests/conflict_gate/fixtures/**/.scp/`). (14) docs/integrations/conflict-gate.md update — verify §'Scope of conflict-gate coverage' accurately describes the new corpus + helper functions. (15) STATUS.md TF-006 closure — verify the strikethrough-and-✅ pattern matches convention; description names the deliverables accurately. NEVER recommend descoping; propose inline-fix or file as TF-020Q-NNN. Output to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020q/review-correctness.json conforming to schemas/sonnet_review_result.schema.json.
